text:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: HOSTED_API_QUEUE_GROWTH -> GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION detected for region-us-east-1. p95 latency spike > 25s, queue depth increasing rapidly. Paging oncall.

Maya P.: I'm seeing huge backlog on /v1/generate across multiple routes. queue_count metric: 42k and climbing. autoscaler logs show repeated allocation failures: \`quota_exceeded\` / \`insufficient_gpus\`.

Diego R.: Confirmed. Metrics snapshot: p50=3.1s p95=28.6s p99=95s. GPU utilization 98% on all hosted pools; some pods OOM-killed due to kvcache memory blowups.

Samir (oncall): I'm on it. Starting mitigation runbook step 1: enable throttling for non-critical routes, reduce max_concurrency for chat endpoints. Pushing patch to rate-limiter.

Priya S.: Heads up — Customer Ops flagged 3 high-tier customers seeing timeouts. CCing Alex.

Alex L. (support): I've opened cases for acme-inc and dataflow-ops. They report 504s and retries. Need ETA asap.

Samir (oncall): Quick actions I took:
- added emergency token-level throttle for free-tier keys
- scaled down default model from \`redwood-13b\` -> \`redwood-6b-q4\` for non-SLA routes via runtime policy
- enabled fallback routing to dedicated-reserved pool for enterprise customers (where config allowed)

sre-runner: autoscaler error trace: ``
2026-06-02T02:00:10Z ERROR allocation_manager.go:129 "Allocation failed" error=\"quota_exceeded: requested 8 gpus, available 0\"
2026-06-02T02:00:11Z WARN pool_controller.go:322 "scale attempt aborted" reason=\"max_pools_reached\"
2026-06-02T02:00:14Z ERROR runtime.go:78 "pod crash" trace=\"oom_kill kvcache\"
``

Maya P.: Where did the quota constraint come from? We had spare quota last week.

Diego R.: Looks like a provider-side soft quota change + some internal reservation for Dedicated trials that unexpectedly consumed capacity. Finance provisioning ticket allocated gpus to dedicated but they never released. I'm opening provider ticket now.

Samir (oncall): While provider responds, putting temporary mitigations: 1) enforce conservative batching (reduce batch_size from 16 -> 6), 2) drop long context requests (truncate to 2k for non-enterprise), 3) prioritize enterprise routing.

Priya S.: Can we run a short canary of fallback model to see quality delta? Ops wants to know risk/rollback.

Samir (oncall): Doing canary to 50 qps on redwood-6b-q4. Logs: 
``
[02:05:12] canary: 50 req/s -> p95 1.8s, increase in hallucination rate minimal in quick evals
``

Maya P.: Good. Continue. Also I pushed a temporary config to enable aggressive prefix caching TTL to 5m for repeat prompts. That should cut load on generation by ~18% according to cache hit sim.

sre-runner: Note: some queued requests are > 2m old and are getting auto-cancelled by client SDKs, causing bursty retry patterns. Recommend enabling jittered retry guidance to SDKs (support email).

Alex L. (support): Noted. Messaging drafted to affected accounts: "We're actively mitigating a capacity issue impacting response times; prioritizing enterprise traffic; may see intermittent 5xx/504s. Engineers working on resolution." Want approval to send.

Priya S.: Send now. Include suggested mitigations and ETA 1-2 hours.

Diego R.: Provider response: "we observed an internal resource reallocation in us-east-1, temporary quota reduction. We can provision +16 GPUs within ~45 minutes if you accept preemptible instances." They also flagged a config mismatch that blocked our autoscaler from requesting the preemptible-compute class.

Samir (oncall): Two parallel tracks: A) get provider to increase quota / allow preemptible pool (accept if SLAs permit), B) keep reducing tail latency and queue via throttles and fallbacks. Can someone update the incident page with mitigations?

Maya P.: I'm updating the incident doc now with actions and timeline. Current mitigation effect: queue growth rate slowed from +6k/min -> +1.2k/min after throttles + model fallback. p95 reduced to ~12s.

sre-runner: Also found autoscaler health check flapping causing scale decisions to abort. Flap发现: health-check timeout 3s too aggressive under high gc. Increasing to 10s. Patch queued to infra.

Samir (oncall): Rolling that health-check change now.

Diego R.: After bumping health-check, we got one successful scale attempt but then hit "max_pools_reached". We can request temporary raise of max_pools to 12 from 8. Who owns that config?

Maya P.: That's infra-config -> putting a patch through emergency change to raise to 12. Need one approval. Priya?

Priya S.: Approved. Apply and monitor.

sre-runner: Change applied. New attempt to allocate succeeded: allocation_manager logs show 8 new GPUs provisioned (preemptible). Queue drained rate improved.

Samir (oncall): Monitoring: queue depth peaked at 46k, now down to 9.6k. p95 trending down toward 6s. Enterprise routing eliminated most timeouts for high-tier customers.

Alex L. (support): Sent customer note to impacted accounts. Received one escalation from acme-inc; offered SLA credit and 1:1 postmortem.

Priya S.: Customer impact summary for status page (short): 
- Impact window: 02:00 - ongoing mitigation (majority mitigated by 02:30)
- Symptom: elevated latency, 5xx/504s for some customers, retry storms
- Severity: SEV2 (enterprise partial degrade)
- Customers: ~125 total affected, 5 high-tier with notable failures

Samir (oncall): Next steps: 1) let pools stabilize, 2) keep throttles in place for 1h, 3) coordinate with provider to convert preemptible -> reserved or release dedicated trials, 4) run replay on queued requests once safe, 5) prepare postmortem.

Maya P.: Handoff to night oncall at 03:00. Leaving runbook notes and list of vendors. If anything spikes back, wake me.

sre-runner: Handoff ack. Current watchlist: queue_depth, p99 latency, autoscaler errors, provider ticket #PRV-1284.

Diego R.: I'll follow up on internal capacity reservation that stole GPUs. Expect update in 2-3 hours.

Samir (oncall): Thanks team. Signing off to sleep handoff.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT: service stabilized to degraded state. Monitoring continues.
